increment: Turned runs 385-386's accident into a method: tools/param_invariance_audit.py, job 51 in selftest_all. Four defects in two components were all found by varying a parameter a selftest held fixed, so this scans every module's selftest for behavioural size parameters exercised at exactly one value. BUILDING THE DETECTOR PRODUCED TWO INSTANCES OF THE DEFECT IT DETECTS. (1) Its vocabulary included 'trials', a Monte Carlo PRECISION parameter that moves only variance, so 9 of 15 first-report rows were noise burying the real hits - a vocabulary not separating the parameters a result depends on from those it does not, which is the failure it was written to find. Precision names now sit under a '~' prefix, unranked; 15 rows -> 7. (2) It could not see a sweep written as 'for k in (3, 20, 50, 100)', only literal ints in range() and kwargs, so it kept flagging executor_pool at range()=3 immediately after that module had been swept over four pool sizes - the detector measuring something other than what the code does, verbatim the run-386 defect. Both visible in the first report in seconds. GENERALISATION: a detector for a defect class is written by someone holding that class's assumptions, the worst position from which to avoid it - but it is cheap to catch, because the detector produces output over a corpus you already know. Run a new detector over the corpus you know best and read the output as a claim about the DETECTOR. Run 380 is the converse (three salient instances felt like a class and were not) and the shared discipline is the cheap check before the confident claim. FIRST REAL OUTPUT: 7 modules, top hit executor_pool at range()=3 - the module run 386 had shown by hand refuses an all-benign 50-worker round while its selftest never built a pool over three. The tool pointed at exactly what a manual audit had had to find. Acted on it: swept 3/20/50/100 with a REGRESSION pin on the k=50 refusal. The tool refuses to overclaim and a selftest asserts it keeps refusing: heuristic surface scan, single-valued is not a bug, swept is not safe, name-based hence non-equivariant. +2 nodes, +7 edges.
